links.note: RETROSPECTIVE: written after the single measurement ran (2026-10-29 ~03:30 UTC); not a preregistration. It records what was done so the export can be bound and reviewed. freeze.filed_before_affected_data is false.

question: On the cloud container, what is the peak anonymous memory of elaborating CryptoResearch.Semaev.BooleanParityDegreeThreeRankCertificate with LEAN_NUM_THREADS=1, and does that setting keep it under the container's limit?

claims.text: With LEAN_NUM_THREADS=1 the elaboration was OOM-killed by the session's memory cgroup at about 339 s with anon-rss 13,520,596 kB, so the module's peak anonymous memory exceeds 13.5 GB (a lower bound) and LEAN_NUM_THREADS=1 does not bring it under a 13.36 GiB cap.
The 2026-10-23 container OOM and the hosted-runner success are explained by this lower bound against the container's 13.36 GiB command cgroup versus ~16 GB on the runner.

arms.description: the same module in the hosted lean-verification job (ubuntu-latest, plain lake build, default Lean threads), observed in job logs 122905972990 (579 s) and 123070123680 (671 s); completed, memory not recorded
lake env lean on the module with LEAN_NUM_THREADS=1, dependencies prebuilt

aa.not_applicable_reason: one run per arm; the claims are an absolute lower bound (C1) and a heuristic explanation (C2), not an arm difference

positive.not_applicable_reason: the kill is confirmed independently by the kernel OOM record (dmesg-oom.txt), which names the process and its anon-rss

negative.not_applicable_reason: no null population; the claim is a lower bound on one deterministic elaboration

factors.name: toolchain
factors.how: lean-toolchain and lake-manifest.json pins; lake exe cache get

comparisons.reason: C1 is an absolute lower bound read from the threads1 run and the kernel OOM record
comparisons.threshold: peak_anon_rss_kb > 13500000 with a CONSTRAINT_MEMCG kill of the lean process

comparisons.reason: host, memory limit and thread setting all differ; used only to frame C2 as a heuristic, never to attribute a difference to one factor

variable_ledger.aa_not_applicable: one run per arm; the reference arm is an existing observation from job logs, not a run of this protocol

seed_derivation.note: Lean elaboration is deterministic; there is no seed

power.note: no statistical test; a lower bound read from one run and the kernel record

preflight_runtime.measured_on: hosted job logs: module 579-671 s; dependency build 236 s here

primary.name: peak anonymous RSS
primary.definition: maximum RssAnon of the lean process over 0.5 s samples, and anon-rss in the kernel OOM record

secondary.name: lean VmHWM
secondary.definition: maximum VmHWM of the lean process

secondary.name: time to OOM kill
secondary.definition: from process start to the last sample before exit

stopping_rules.rule: one run of the threads1 arm, stop when the process exits or is killed (decided before running; not written down until this retrospective record)

invalidation_rules: a kill by the sampler's own watchdog would make the peak a lower bound set by the watchdog, not the limit; it did not fire

decision_rule.text: C1 holds if the kernel OOM record names the lean process with anon-rss above 13.5 GB under CONSTRAINT_MEMCG (C-bound). C-host is confounded and decides nothing; C2 stays a heuristic estimate.

inadmissible: reading the lower bound as the module's peak
reading the 13.36 GiB cap as the hosted runner's limit
reading the timed value as a performance claim
